$comment: Chain claims-sibling convention as in del-mh-001 (parallel chain_claims array; __COMPUTED_CHAIN_HASH__). The revocation snapshot is a JCS-profile artifact (unchanged by the JWS migration); its signature placeholder __VALID_B_SIG__ is minted by B over the JCS-canonical revocation_list bytes.
description: Multi-hop per-hop revocation (RFC-AITP-0011 §6, aitp/0.2 shape). The chain (identical to del-mh-001) is structurally valid: every hop's JWS verifies, the voucher inside chain[0] verifies under A's own key, continuity, expiry monotonicity, transitive scope subsetting, and chain_hash recomputation all pass. However, B's signed revocation snapshot (B = chain[0].iss) lists chain[0].jti = 550e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655443002 in `entries`. Per RFC-AITP-0011 §6, the verifier MUST look up every hop token's jti against the deny list of that hop's iss (and chain[0].voucher.src_jti against A's own deny list), after all signature checks (RFC-AITP-0008 §3.3); a revocation hit at ANY hop invalidates the entire delegation. Expected: DELEGATION_SOURCE_TCT_REVOKED.

expected.rationale: chain[0].jti (550e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655443002) is in the deny list of chain[0].iss (B). Per RFC-AITP-0011 §6, every hop token's jti is checked against that hop issuer's deny list; a hit at any hop invalidates the entire delegation, after all signature checks have passed.
